citation: Linaugo, J. D., Alcala, E. L., Bucol, A. A., Menes, C. C., Pacalioga, J. O., Turbanos, F. M., & Patiluna, M. L. E. (2010). An Annotated Checklist on the Introduced Aquatic Fauna of Two River Systems on Negros and Panay, Philippines. Silliman Journal, 51(1), beginning at p. 138.

scopeReview.sourceReportedScope: Annotated list of 16 introduced aquatic fauna, including 11 fish, three herptiles and two mollusks. The abstract names three fish as apparently new introduced records in the two river systems but does not assign them separately to each river.
scopeReview.stationCoverage: Publisher-PDF search indexing shows four Bago River stations and three Jalaur River stations in Figure 1; the full figure, methods and station text were not reviewed directly.
scopeReview.targetCatalogFit: The fish component is a candidate Visayas freshwater source. Herptile and mollusk taxa are outside the current fish catalog.

accessAndRights.directPublisherPdf: Repeated retrieval failed; only search-indexed excerpts were available.
accessAndRights.pidsDownload: Requires a security verification; not completed.
accessAndRights.license: No open license identified. Silliman Journal states copyright is held by the journal and individual authors; reproduction permission is required for a full article, over 500 words of text, or two or more tables/figures.

decision.use: Bibliographic and taxon-source discovery lead only
decision.reason: The source potentially supplies two river systems and seven sampled stations, but the fish list, taxon-to-river mapping, survey dates, collection methods and specimen evidence were not directly reviewed. Copyright/reuse remains unapproved.

limitations: The Silliman platform's page shows a 2022 publication date while identifying its issue as Silliman Journal 51(1) (2010); the issue metadata and PIDS record identify the work as 2010. Treat 2022 as a platform metadata date, not a new edition.
The abstract says introduced aquatic fauna, not that every listed fish is invasive or currently established.
A river-level abstract does not establish which taxon was recorded in which system or station.
No species list, coordinates, geometry, current occurrence, native/introduced decision, safety, catchability or fishing-rule claim is created by this review.
nextActions: Use a legitimately accessible publisher or library copy; do not bypass the PIDS security verification.
If full text is obtained, transcribe source names separately from modern taxonomy and preserve taxon-to-river/station links only where explicitly reported.
Check each introduced-status claim against current taxonomic and non-native-species authorities before any separate public status display.
Confirm article/table reuse terms before reproducing any table or structured taxon data in the public app.
